content: 1. Fentanyl and linezolid can each increase the toxicity of the other by elevating serotonin levels. This combination should be avoided, or alternative drugs should be used. If fentanyl (intranasal, transdermal, or transmucosal) is required, monitor for serotonin toxicity. 2. Linezolid and fluoxetine both increase serotonin levels and are contraindicated together. Linezolid may elevate serotonin due to its MAO-A inhibition. If linezolid must be administered, discontinue serotonergic drugs immediately and monitor for CNS toxicity. Serotonergic therapy can be resumed 24 hours after the last linezolid dose or after 5 weeks of monitoring, whichever comes first. 3. Linezolid and fluphenazine have an unspecified interaction mechanism. Use caution and monitor closely. Serotonin modulators may enhance dopamine blockade, increasing the risk of neuroleptic malignant syndrome. Antipsychotics may enhance serotonergic effects, potentially leading to serotonin syndrome. Monitor for signs of serotonin toxicity (e.g., mental status changes, autonomic instability, neuromuscular hyperactivity) or neuroleptic malignant syndrome (e.g., hyperthermia, muscle rigidity, autonomic dysfunction). 4. Linezolid and fluvoxamine both increase serotonin levels. Avoid this combination or use alternative drugs. 5. Linezolid increases the effects of formoterol through pharmacodynamic synergism, which may lead to an acute hypertensive episode. This combination is contraindicated. 6. Linezolid and frovatriptan both increase serotonin levels. Avoid this combination or use alternative drugs. If linezolid must be administered, discontinue serotonergic drugs immediately and monitor for CNS toxicity. Linezolid may also increase frovatriptan levels by decreasing its metabolism. 7. Linezolid and gepirone both increase serotonin levels. Use caution and monitor for symptoms of serotonin syndrome when gepirone is used with other drugs affecting serotonergic neurotransmitter systems. Gepirone is contraindicated in patients taking MAOIs, including linezolid or IV methylene blue, or in those who have taken MAOIs within the preceding 14 days. Allow at least 14 days after stopping gepirone before starting an MAOI. 8. Linezolid increases the effects of glimepiride, glipizide, glyburide, and various forms of insulin (e.g., aspart, detemir, glargine, glulisine, lispro, NPH, regular human) by unknown mechanisms. Use caution and monitor closely. 9. Linezolid and green tea may interact, increasing the risk of cardiac arrhythmias or severe hypertension due to the caffeine component of green tea. Avoid excessive consumption of green tea or its combination with linezolid. 10. Linezolid and haloperidol have an unspecified interaction mechanism. Use caution and monitor closely. Serotonin modulators may enhance dopamine blockade, increasing the risk of neuroleptic malignant syndrome. Antipsychotics may enhance serotonergic effects, potentially leading to serotonin syndrome. Monitor for signs of serotonin toxicity or neuroleptic malignant syndrome. 11. Linezolid increases the toxicity of hydrocodone and hydromorphone by elevating serotonin levels. Avoid this combination or use alternative drugs. MAOI interactions with opioids may manifest as serotonin syndrome or opioid toxicity (e.g., respiratory depression, coma). If urgent opioid treatment is needed, use test doses and frequent titration of small doses while closely monitoring blood pressure and signs of CNS and respiratory depression. 12. Linezolid increases the effects of iloperidone, loxapine, and loxapine inhaled by unspecified mechanisms. Use caution and monitor closely. Serotonin modulators may enhance dopamine blockade, increasing the risk of neuroleptic malignant syndrome. Antipsychotics may enhance serotonergic effects, potentially leading to serotonin syndrome. Monitor for signs of serotonin toxicity or neuroleptic malignant syndrome. 13. Linezolid and imipramine both increase serotonin levels. Avoid this combination or use alternative drugs. 14. Linezolid decreases the level or effect of iobenguane I-131 by interfering with catecholamine uptake into cells, reducing iobenguane efficacy. Discontinue interfering drugs for at least 5 half-lives before administering iobenguane. Do not administer these drugs until at least 7 days after each iobenguane dose. 15. Linezolid and isocarboxazid both increase serotonin levels. Avoid this combination or use alternative drugs. 16. Linezolid and isometheptene increase each other's effects through pharmacodynamic synergism. This combination is contraindicated due to the risk of hypertension and ventricular tachycardia. 17. Linezolid and isoniazid both increase serotonin levels. Avoid this combination or use alternative drugs. 18. Linezolid increases the effects of isoproterenol through pharmacodynamic synergism, which may lead to an acute hypertensive episode. This combination is contraindicated. 19. Linezolid increases the levels of ketamine through pharmacodynamic synergism. Use caution and monitor closely. 20. Linezolid and L-tryptophan both increase serotonin levels. Avoid this combination or use alternative drugs. 21. Linezolid increases the effects of lasmiditan by elevating serotonin levels. Use caution and monitor closely, as coadministration may increase the risk of serotonin syndrome. 22. Linezolid and levalbuterol increase each other's effects through pharmacodynamic synergism, which may lead to an acute hypertensive episode. This combination is contraindicated. 23. Linezolid and levodopa both increase serotonin levels. Avoid this combination or use alternative drugs. Coadministration of selective MAO-B inhibitors with levodopa may be associated with orthostatic hypotension. 24. Linezolid and levomilnacipran both increase serotonin levels. Avoid this combination or use alternative drugs. 25. Linezolid increases the toxicity of levorphanol by unknown mechanisms. Avoid this combination or use alternative drugs. 26. Linezolid and lisdexamfetamine increase each other's effects through pharmacodynamic synergism. This combination is contraindicated due to the risk of an acute hypertensive episode. 27. Linezolid and lithium both increase serotonin levels. Avoid this combination or use alternative drugs. Linezolid may increase serotonin due to its MAO-A inhibition. If linezolid must be administered, discontinue serotonergic drugs immediately and monitor for CNS toxicity. 28. Linezolid and lofepramine both increase serotonin levels. This combination is contraindicated. 29. Linezolid and lorcaserin both increase serotonin levels. Avoid this combination or use alternative drugs. 30. Linezolid and maprotiline both increase serotonin levels. Avoid this combination or use alternative drugs. 31. Linezolid increases the toxicity of meperidine by unknown mechanisms. Avoid this combination or use alternative drugs. If linezolid must be administered, discontinue serotonergic drugs immediately and monitor for CNS toxicity. 32. Linezolid decreases the level or effect of mestranol by altering intestinal flora. This applies only to oral forms of the hormone. There is a low risk of contraceptive failure. Use caution and monitor closely. 33. Linezolid increases the effects of metaproterenol through pharmacodynamic synergism, which may lead to an acute hypertensive episode. This combination is contraindicated. 34. Linezolid increases the level or effect of metformin by unknown mechanisms. Use caution and monitor closely.
